brief: A compact desk unit with a drawer, plus a spike at a corner where three bases meet to hold a small platform.

requirements.evidence: Four hex bases: full bases at (0,0), (1,0), (0,1) and a west half-base at (-1,0) form a compact cluster; the open faces are closed with solid caps and joints bolted (lockJoints). check_build is ok with meshClash clear.
notch:0#-1,1 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf, drawer frame) fills the empty position between bases (0,1) and (-1,0).

requirements.requirement: Spike at a corner where three bases meet
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 (mount variant) sits at the junction of bases (0,0), (0,1) and (1,0). The default spike type refused a platform, so I swapped it for a mount type.
setSpikeAccessory platform-sm on that spike at level 0 applied without refusal. No props were added, so the platform is the accessory itself, not a dressed object.

finish.summary: Built a compact four-base desk unit with a notch drawer frame between two bases, and a mount-type spike at the three-base corner carrying a small platform. Caps close the open faces, joints are locked, and the check reports no issues with mesh clash clear. I did not verify the drawer's pull-out or the platform's load, and material suitability is not covered by the configurator.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
